Reading from standard input

Zuguang Gu (guzuguang@suat-sz.edu.cn)

2026-11-24

pipe.Rmd
## Warning: package 'knitr' was built under R version 4.6.1

Reading from standard input fromm upstream command is basically to support special flags. In the following example, the argument input expects a file or a flag representing standard input.

library(argitect)
argitect(
    "input=s", "input"
)

if(input %in% c("-", "stdin")) {
    cat(readLines(file("stdin")), sep = "\n")
} else {
    cat(readLines(input), sep = "\n")
}

Then from command-line, standard input can be set via - or stdin:

~\> echo hello | Rscript pipe.R --input -
~\> echo hello | Rscript pipe.R --input stdin
hello

input can also be set as a positional argument, then no argument name is needed to specify on the command-line.

library(argitect)
argitect(
    "input=s#", "input"
)

if(input %in% c("-", "stdin")) {
    cat(readLines(file("stdin")), sep = "\n")
} else {
    cat(readLines(input), sep = "\n")
}
~\> cat main.R | Rscript pipe.R -
~\> cat main.R | Rscript pipe.R stdin

main.R is the script we used in vignette Dispatching to sub-commands.

library(argitect)

sub_commands(
    system.file("extdata", "sub1.R", package = "argitect"), "This is the description of sub command 1, which will be a long long long text.",
    system.file("extdata", "sub2.R", package = "argitect"), "This is the description of sub command 2, which will be a long long long text."
)
